output.title: The quiet cost of model deprecation
output.body:
If you are comparing automation with another hire, the quiet cost is not the first build. It is what happens when the model underneath the workflow changes, gets retired, or is priced in a way that makes the setup awkward to keep.

For a small business, that can show up in ordinary work like customer-inquiry triage, lead qualification, or invoice handling. A workflow may look fine on day one and still need attention later if the underlying model changes. That is not a disaster, but it is a maintenance decision, and it belongs in the business case from the start.

The practical next step is simple: before you approve an automation pilot, ask one blunt question. If the underlying model is upgraded, retired, or repriced, does the workflow keep working, or will it need to be rebuilt and reviewed again by a human before any money moves?

If that answer is unclear, you do not have a finished plan yet. You have a hopeful sketch. The cheapest entry price is not always the cheapest workflow.
